result.title: HiMEM: Hippocampus-Inspired Memory Consolidation, Pruning, and Composition for Vision-Language-Action Models in 3D Scenes
result.summary: Memory plays a crucial role in long-horizon task execution and cross-task generalization for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models operating in complex 3D scenes. However, existing VLA memory mechanisms suffer from memory noise, particularly in complex 3D scenes, as stored episodic memories contain extensive redundant details about scene layouts, object configurations, and robot-specific states, which obscure generalizable manipulation principles and hinder cross-task transfer. To address this challenge, we first introduce a hippocampus-inspired memory consolidation mechanism that synthesizes extensive episodic experiences into a compact set of essential semantic memories, enabling VLA models to derive generalizable principles from practical experience. Second, we propose an episodic memory pruning mechanism that removes redundant episodic memories whose contents are captured by consolidated semantic memories, thereby increasing effective memory capacity and improving long-horizon task execution. Finally, to handle complex task scenarios, we develop a flexible memory composition mechanism that jointly leverages multiple episodic and semantic memories to enhance cross-scenario generalization. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus demonstrate the effectiveness of HiMEM across different VLA backbones, improving the average success rate of pi_0 from 91.88% to 98.20% on LIBERO.

AI.brief_summary: 面向 3D 场景中的 VLA 模型，提出受海马体启发的记忆机制：将大量情节记忆整合为紧凑的语义记忆，剪除已被语义记忆覆盖的冗余情节记忆，并灵活组合多类记忆以提升长程任务执行与跨任务泛化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「情节记忆→紧凑语义记忆」的整合与冗余剪除，与 LVR 中状态抽象、信息坍缩和冗余视觉证据筛选的问题表述可能相通，可供核查记忆压缩是否改善推理状态质量；但工作聚焦机器人操作的外部记忆库，与推理期 latent 状态生成无直接对应。
